newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-GERMAN OPEN A TEST FOR WOOSNAM -- AND THE COURSE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GERMAN OPEN A TEST FOR WOOSNAM -- AND THE COURSE.

text.p: Briton Ian Woosnam will aim to bounce back from an indifferent U.S. Open last week when he defends his title in the German Open which starts on Thursday.
But this Stuttgart course will have something to prove as well.

While Woosnam won Europe's top event of the year so far, the PGA Championship, less than a month ago, and is leading the Tour rankings, he missed the cut at the U.S. Open and will be intent on showing that was merely a blip.
Last year here Woosnam won over 54 holes in a rain-affected event and was one of several players who criticised the layout as being too easy.
The 36-hole qualifying cut-off came at five-under-par, the lowest of the year, and the Welshman was already 20 under par when storms prevented the leaders starting the final round.

European Ryder Cup captain Severiano Ballesteros, despite missing the cut by a stroke, was another of the critics, maintaining the course gave a false sense of achievement to potential Cup team players.
The European Tour has responded by making changes aimed at toughening the course, keeping the par at 71 but increasing the length by 102 yards to 6,850, adding several bunkers and adjusting 11 holes.

"In addition, the programme to grow rough has been relatively successful," said tournament director Andy McFee, "and although the fairways remain fair targets the penalty for missing them is far more severe."
Bernhard Langer, who helped design the course, is likely to be one of Woosnam's biggest threats as the German seeks his sixth win in this event.
Italy's Costantino Rocca, returning after injury forced his withdrawal from the U.S. Open, will be attempting to halt his slide down the European Ryder Cup points table.

A member of the Ryder Cup team in the last two matches against the United States, Rocca has slipped to ninth place in the standings and with only the top 10 gaining automatic selection will be desperate for a high placed finish.
